simple.meaning: עַכְשׁוּב (ʻakshûwb) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an asp (from lurking coiled up).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Psalms 140:4. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַכְשׁוּב (H5919) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H5919. akshub עַכְשׁוּב noun masculine usually asp, viper (so ᵑ9 ᵐ5 ; perhaps conject. from sense and || נָחָשׁ ), but perhaps = (? corrupt for) עַכָּבִישׁ spider (q. v.; compare ᵑ7 on the passage ); — ע ׳חֲמַת Psa 140:4 a viper's (? spider's) venom is under their lips (see especially Che and references). עַל see עֹל עלה see III. עלל .
definitions.rootNote: probably from an unused root meaning to coil ;

occurrences.englishText: Yahweh, keep me from the hands of the wicked.
